name: Icon button
summary: A button with only an icon, such as closing the sheet or going back. It always has an accessible name, and a 44px target however small its icon.

when: For actions everyone recognises from the icon alone: close, back, and show or hide a password.
Where space is tight, such as the sheet's header.

whenNot.text: When the icon alone could be misread.
whenNot.instead: Button, with the icon beside a label

anatomy.description: The area people press: at least 44px by 44px, even when it looks smaller.
Decorative: the button's label names it.

props.name: label
props.description: Its accessible name, such as “Close”. Required, because the icon alone has no name. Pass a catalogue string.

states.name: Default
states.description: Just the icon, on no background.

states.name: Hover
states.description: A round background appears behind the icon.

states.name: Focus
states.description: A 2px focus ring around the round target.

events.name: click
events.when: It's pressed, by pointer, keyboard or assistive technology.

accessibility.name: Its label prop. The icon is hidden from screen readers.
screenReader: Announced as a button, with its label, such as “Close, button”.
notes: Its target is at least 44px by 44px (WCAG 2.5.5), even beside a 20px icon.
The icon keeps its colour in forced colours, so it stays visible.

related.relationship: When a label is clearer than an icon.

guidelines: Name it after what it does, not what it shows: “Close”, not “X”.
Use the same name for the same action everywhere.

dosAndDonts.do: Give it a label that says what it does.
dosAndDonts.dont: Leave it unnamed, or name it after the icon.

evidence.point: A button with no accessible name is announced as just “button”.
The prototype's 36px icon buttons were too small; the target is now 44px.
